claims.text: A method of scoring a learner's performance by computing a plurality of behavioral/interaction-derived parameters, applying a weighting profile selected according to a declared or inferred disability classification, excluding from the weighted composite any parameter for which a more severe form of the classified condition would mechanically depress the parameter independent of learning outcome, renormalizing the remaining weights over the parameters actually measurable for the given session, and reporting a coverage value indicating what fraction of the profile's intended weight was measured.

elements.text: Per-disability weight profiles, loaded from versioned config.
Diagnostic-only exclusion — computed and reported, never scored.
Weighted composite with renormalization over present parameters and a reported coverage fraction.
A teacher may override a specific student's weight profile, with a mandatory logged reason, without altering the diagnostic-only exclusion rule.

claims.text: A method of classifying the probable cause of an incorrect learner response by comparing the response's latency against that specific learner's own historical response-time baseline (never a cohort or population baseline) in combination with a face-presence signal, producing a labelled classification with an associated confidence value and, where two causes are indistinguishable on the available signals, abstaining to a default label while recording the alternative causes rather than selecting one by default.

elements.text: Four-way cause classification with confidence and recorded alternatives.
Abstention when the face-presence signal is absent or has too few samples to trust.
Server-side re-classification at ingest from stored raw signals, independent of client-supplied labels, versioned so a formula change relabels old events without a backfill migration.

claims.text: A method of serving a pre-generated, profile-constrained simpler variant of a learning item immediately upon classifying an incorrect response as a comprehension barrier at or above a confidence threshold, tracking the re-presented attempt as a distinct event correlated to the original item rather than overwriting the original record.

elements.text: Frontend closed loop — classify, swap the item in place, track the re-presentation as a distinct attempt.
elements.code_detail: ok (textual match only — no TS compiler available to this script)

claims.text: A method of computing a non-clinical, interaction-only resilience signal from a combination of: response latency relative to the learner's own baseline, frequency of response revision, frequency of input-focus loss, and a mean sentiment score derived from a conversational support interface, where the signal's constituent weights are renormalized over whichever inputs are available for a given session rather than requiring all four.

elements.text: Weight-renormalizing hesitation index over 1-4 available interaction signals.
Per-session aggregation of the four input signals into the index.

claims.text: A method of presenting a machine-generated, multi-step numeric solution to a learner in which each proposed step is independently re-evaluated by a deterministic, restricted expression evaluator before being displayed, such that a step whose claimed result does not match independent re-evaluation is discarded rather than shown, combined with a deterministic (non-generative) typing of the conceptual or procedural cause of an incorrect numeric response.

elements.text: Restricted-grammar expression evaluator (no eval/sympify on model output).
Per-step independent re-verification; an unverifiable step is dropped, never shown.
Deterministic error typing from the structural relationship between the correct and given answers.

claims.text: A method of scoring a learner's free-form written response along two independent axes — concept coverage and written-expression quality — in which concept coverage is computed deterministically from a machine-identified evidentiary span that is independently verified to appear verbatim in the learner's own response (a claimed match that fails this verification is rejected regardless of the machine's own assertion), and the written-expression axis is excluded from any composite score for a condition whose more severe form would mechanically depress it.

elements.text: Independent written-expression rubric score, excluded from the composite for the relevant profile.
